A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Multipole Semantic Attention by the same authors. All 17 pages of v3 and 21 pages of v4, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original pretraining experiments, attention microbenchmarks, Llama evaluations, ablations and downstream results, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds retrieval and code-completion evaluations, runtime profiling and further ablations.

M1.justification: v3 already stops gradients through query centroids. v4 adds an optional variant stopping gradients through tilted aggregation weights with respect to the query centroid and keys, while retaining gradients through aggregated keys (Appendix C). This changes training for that variant; the main algorithm and headline experiments retain the earlier procedure.

E1.justification: v4 adds RULER retrieval tasks, custom cross-file code retrieval with single-needle, multi-key and multi-query variants, and LongBench code completion on RepoBench-P and LCC. These substantially extend task requirements beyond the retained language-modeling, PG-19, ARC-Easy and SciQ evaluations. Training corpora remain unchanged.

E2.justification: CUDNN/Pallas Flash, MoBA, block-diagonal attention and existing clustering controls remain in their corresponding comparisons. Added downstream benchmarks compare the existing CUDNN- and MuSe-trained regimes. The new aggregation-gradient variant is an ablation of the proposed method.

E3.justification: New protocols include 64k-context RULER evaluation with 500 examples per cell, custom retrieval scored by uid exact match with controlled or randomly sampled needle depths, and LongBench edit similarity. Appendix F.2 adds a controlled eight-pair retrieval-budget sweep. Existing pretraining and PG-19 settings are retained; these are additional protocols, not demonstrated reruns under revised settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds an aggregation-gradient ablation testing adaptation to approximate attention, component runtime profiling, and a fixed-budget comparison of semantic versus spatial retrieval breadth. Appendix G.4 additionally analyzes custom retrieval accuracy by needle depth. These address mechanisms, computational bottlenecks and sensitivity beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: v3 gives an approximate standard error for ARC-Easy/SciQ. v4 additionally reports binomial standard errors for custom NIAH and RULER, explicitly documents the RULER uncertainty calculation, and reports harness-provided standard errors for LongBench (Tables 9, 10 and 31). No increase in training seeds or repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Headline pretraining and existing baseline results are retained, but substantial new results appear. Table 11 reports 0.6991 exact-attention loss for the new gradient variant. Custom multi-key 4× retrieval reaches 97.36% for MuSe versus 81.50% for CUDNN training (Table 9), whereas scientific-domain RULER niah_multikey_1 favors CUDNN, 50.4% versus 28.0% (Table 31). LongBench, runtime-component, retrieval-breadth and depth-resolved results are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Appendix B expands the earlier dipole derivation into a substantive error analysis. New Equations 10–15 derive expected value error, a factorized variance bound, within- versus between-cluster responses, and errors from merging or sharing covariance corrections. The earlier claim that K-means exactly minimizes the error is qualified through isotropy and tilted-versus-untilted covariance caveats.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: separate query/key clustering, retrieval-augmented approximation, approximately 2× attention speedup, 36% pretraining throughput improvement and preserved quality/interchangeability. Explicitly calling MuSe a training-time approximation clarifies the existing pretraining focus; the added experiments principally support retained claims.

C2.justification: v4 supplements the earlier regularization/adaptation explanation with a specific aggregation-gradient mechanism. It adds interpretations of runtime bottlenecks, early-training behavior and situations requiring greater spatial retrieval breadth. It also attributes poor RULER performance to domain shift and limited instruction following, while acknowledging these factors were not disentangled. The suggested GQA optimization changes from sharing summaries to sharing key clustering.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies per-forward-pass recomputation without persistent state and use of MuSe from the first training step without attention warmup. It clarifies the existing layer-count choice and approximately 1.1 code-training epochs, and documents clustering operation counts. Appendix I newly states that research code accompanies the OpenReview submission. These are documentation/access additions; core hardware and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to LongBench, RULER and Greengard and Rokhlin's particle-simulation work. The positioning relative to existing efficient-attention methods remains stable. Other reference changes largely correct bibliographic information or update publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact. v4 adds local clarifications and conference front matter, retitles and expands Appendix B, moves downstream discussion into Section 4.3, promotes distributed-training discussion from G.4 to H, and adds impact and code-availability sections. The expansion primarily supplies new scientific content rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables 5, 9–11, 21 and 31–32 introduce substantial new displays covering runtime components, benchmarks, ablations and depth sensitivity, including sample-count, uncertainty and grouped comparison columns. All six figures are retained unchanged. Earlier tables largely retain their structure and values while being relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 supported long-context capability mainly through loss and approximation measurements; v4 adds direct retrieval and code-completion evidence, including unfavorable RULER outcomes. Expanded Appendix B supplies important error arguments and qualifies the clustering justification. Together these substantially strengthen empirical validation and mathematical explanation. The gradient variant remains preliminary and the RULER causal interpretation unverified, but these limitations do not outweigh the added evidence and transparency.
